Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 13 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi Releases Rs 1,000 Crore PMEGP Subsidy to Support 11,333 Micro Enterprises In October 2026, Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi, Minister of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), released Rs.1,000 crore as Margin Money (MM) subsidy under the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) to support 11,333 new micro enterprises across India. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Release of Margin Money subsidy under PMEGP ✓ Who? Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi, MoMSME ✓ About PMEGP: ✓ Administered by: MoMSME ✓ Implemented by: KVIC ✓ Nature: Central Sector Scheme; credit-linked subsidy programme. ✓ Objective: Employment generation through new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. About Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP): Launch: PMEGP is a major credit-linked subsidy programme and Central Sector Scheme introduced in August 2008 to generate sustainable employment opportunities through the establishment of new micro- enterprises in the non-farm sector across rural and urban areas. Merger of Earlier Schemes: The programme was introduced by merging two erstwhile schemes, namely the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) and the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP), which were in operation until 31 March 2008. Administration and Implementation: PMEGP is administered by the MoMSME and implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), the national-level nodal agency. Eligibility Criteria: Applicants must be above 18 years of age. A minimum Class VIII qualification is required for projects costing above Rs.10 lakh in the manufacturing sector and Rs.5 lakh in the business/service sector. Implementation Mechanism: Subsidy Disbursement: The KVIC acts as the national-level nodal agency, implementing PMEGP through State KVIC Directorates, State KVIBs, District Industries Centres (DICs), Coir Board and participating banks. The MM Subsidy is routed through KVIC to participating banks and adjusted against beneficiaries’ loan accounts as per scheme guidelines. Financial Assistance under PMEGP: Project Cost: PMEGP provides credit-linked financial assistance for establishing new micro-enterprises, with a maximum admissible project cost of Rs.50 lakh for the manufacturing sector and Rs.20 lakh for the business/service sector. • General Category: 15% subsidy (Urban), 25% (Rural); beneficiary contribution: 10%. • Special Category: 25% subsidy (Urban), 35% (Rural); beneficiary contribution: 5%. • Special Categories: SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities, women, ex-servicemen, transgender persons, differently abled persons and beneficiaries from the North-Eastern Region (NER), Aspirational Districts, and notified hill and border areas. Achievements under PMEGP: Since Financial Year 2014–15 (FY15): Established over 8.38 lakh micro-enterprises, generated

Exam Hints ✓ What? NSO releases PLFS July-September 2026 ✓ LFPR: 55.5%, Rural – 58.1%, Urban – 50.4% ✓ WPR: 52.7%, Rural – 55.6%, Urban – 46.9% ✓ UR – 5.1%, Rural – 4.3%, Urban – 6.8% ✓ Rural employment shares: Primary – 56.7%, Secondary – 21.9%, Tertiary – 21.4%. Sample Data: PLFS: It was launched in April 2017, PLFS assesses employment and unemployment trends in India. Revamped in January 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly rural–urban estimates, its July–September 2026 report marks the 6th quarterly bulletin. • Key indicators include Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR), measured using Current Weekly Status (CWS) based on the preceding seven days. Sample Size: At the all-India level, the quarterly estimates are based on information collected from a total of 5,55,593 persons surveyed. • 2,38,910 persons surveyed in urban area • 3,16,683 persons surveyed in rural area Employed Population: Using the projected population figures provided by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the absolute number of workers aged 15 years and above was estimated at an average of: • 57.9 crore (Cr) during July-September 2026, comprising 40.5 Cr males and 17.4 Cr females. Key Findings: Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR): The overall LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above

BANKING & FINANCE RBI Issues Cybersecurity Directions for Non-Bank PSOs with 6-Hour Incident Reporting, Launches Three Key Surveys In November 2026, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued Master Directions (MD) on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank Payment System Operators (PSO), tightening the cybersecurity protocols and mandating a strict six-hour incident reporting window for payment entities. • The directions were issued under Section 10(2), read with Section 18, of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007. • The RBI announces the launch of three key surveys to capture inflation expectations and consumer confidence. Exam Hints: ✓ What? RBI issues cybersecurity directions for non-bank PSOs and launches three surveys ✓ Legal Basis: Sections 10(2) and 18 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 ✓ Applicable To: Authorised non-bank PSOs ✓ Incident Reporting Deadline: Within 6 hours of detection ✓ Effective From: 5 November 2026 for large and medium PSOs; 1 April 2028 for small PSOs ✓ Cooling-off period: Minimum 12 hours ✓ Three Surveys Launched: IESH, UCCS and RCCS o Purpose of Surveys: Provide inputs for RBI’s monetary policy o IESH & UCCS Coverage: 19 cities each o RCCS Coverage: Rural and semi-urban areas across 31 States/UTs. RBI Cybersecurity Framework for PSOs: Effective From: The master directions take effect immediately (November 5, 2026) for large and medium non-bank PSOs, while small payment operators have been granted a compliance window extending until April 1, 2028. Objective: The directions aim to improve safety and security of the payment systems operated by PSOs by providing a framework for overall information security preparedness with an emphasis on cyber resilience. Reporting Time: PSOs must notify the RBI and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) within six hours of detecting unusual incidents, including cyberattacks, critical system outages, internal frauds, or settlement delays Responsibility: The board of each payment operator will be responsible for overseeing information security risks, including cyber risks and resilience. • Boards may delegate primary oversight to a sub-committee, which must meet at least once every quarter.

# Page 18^page=18
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 18 Daily Content PDF Policy: PSOs must formulate a Board-approved Information Security Policy, review it annually, and prepare a separate Cyber Crisis Management Plan to address cyber threats and attacks. Annual Audit Report: Authorised PSOs must file an annual System Audit Report (SAR): • By 1st June – For entities which follow an April-March financial year • By 1st March – For entities which follow Calendar Year Corrective Actions: The SAR and compliance status must be placed before the entity’s Board, with time- bound corrective actions, maximum 3 months for open observations and progress reported to the RBI. Cooling Off Period: Whenever there is a change in registered mobile number or email ID linked to the payment instrument there shall be a cooling period of minimum 12 hours before allowing any payment transaction through online modes / channels. PSO Classification: Large PSOs include the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), card networks, White Label ATM Operators (WLAOs), Payment Aggregators (PAs), Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) operators and large Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI) issuers. • Medium PSOs include medium PPI issuers and specified cross-border money transfer operators, while small PSOs cover small PPI issuers and instant money transfer operators. RBI Announces Launch of Three Key Surveys: In November 2026, the RBI announced the launch of three key surveys to capture inflation expectations of households and evaluate consumer confidence in the country. Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH): The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets. • The study will be conducted across 19 cities -Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Bengaluru (Karnataka), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Chandigarh (Chandigarh), Chennai (Tamil Nadu, TN), Delhi (Delhi), Guwahati (Assam), Hyderabad (Telangana), Jaipur (Rajasthan), Jammu (Jammu & Kashmir, J&K), Kolkata (West Bengal, WB), Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh, UP), Mumbai (Maharashtra), Nagpur (Maharashtra), Patna (Bihar), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Ranchi (Jharkhand) and Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala). • The survey will be conducted by Hansa Research Group Private Limited. Urban Consumer Confidence Survey (UCCS): This survey gathers qualitative responses from households on their assessment of the general economic situation, employment prospects, price levels, income and spending. • This survey will also be conducted across the same 19 cities. • The survey will be conducted by Hansa Research Group Private Limited. Rural Consumer Confidence Survey (RCCS): This captures households’ current perceptions and one-year- ahead expectations on the overall economic situation, employment conditions, price levels, income and spending. • It will cover rural and semi-urban households across 31 states and Union Territories (UTs). • The survey will be conducted by Ipsos Research Private Limited. IRDAI Constituted Two Working Groups to Prepare RBC Framework Aligned with Ind-AS On 10 November 2026, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) constituted two working groups, one each for life and non-life insurance, to develop a Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework aligned with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS). • The initiative aims to transition India’s insurance sector from the existing factor-based solvency regime to a risk-sensitive capital framework, ensuring financial stability and policyholder protection. Exam Hints ✓ What? Constitution of Two Working Groups for RBC Framework CCWM1.5NiGZzDcNxkqPjJtBkmEDCkZAJ8uFTUHE1VrU9EIi4MZHDtUg2J9CoPqv3vpaZZVDkgbVZxgBgD1Ffklpgesca31fdNzVw

# Page 19^page=19
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 19 Daily Content PDF ✓ Constituted By: IRDAI ✓ Number of Groups: 2 (Life and Non-Life Insurance) ✓ Life Group Convener: Jamuna Choudhary ✓ Non-Life Group Convener: Parmeshwar Shelke ✓ Framework: Risk-Based Capital (RBC) ✓ Aligned With: Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) ✓ Deadline: Within One Month ✓ Key Deliverables: Exposure Draft of RBC Regulations and Approach Paper Working Group to Prepare New Framework RBC Framework: IRDAI plans to introduce a Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework in place of the existing factor-based solvency system. • This approach will ensure that insurance companies maintain capital reserves in proportion to the risks associated with their operations. Factor-Based Solvency System: In this system, capital requirements are calculated using pre-determined factors or percentages applied to an insurer’s premiums, claims and liabilities, rather than fully considering its individual risk profile. Ind AS: The proposed approach will use Ind AS statements as the basis for the RBC balance sheet. Objective: The objective is to avoid maintaining two separate and disconnected systems for financial reporting and solvency assessment. Composition of Working Groups: Life Insurance Group: Convened by Jamuna Choudhary, the 13-member group includes chief financial officers (CFOs) or appointed actuaries from the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), SBI Life, HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life, Bajaj Life, Tata AIA, Kotak Life, Bandhan Life and Aditya Birla Life, along with Munich Re and the Institute of Actuaries of India. Non-Life Insurance Group: Convened by Parmeshwar Shelke, the 12-member group includes representatives from New India Assurance, ICICI Lombard, Bajaj General, SBI General, Tata AIG, Niva Bupa, IndusInd General and Kiwi General, along with Swiss Re and the Institute of Actuaries of India. Areas of Examination: The working groups will examine various aspects of the proposed framework, including: • Valuation of insurers’ assets and liabilities. • Determination of available capital and required capital. • Classification of capital into different tiers. • Identification and measurement of different risk categories. • Calculation of capital requirements after considering risk aggregation and diversification benefits. • Treatment of debt securities, expected credit losses (ECL), contractual service margin (CSM), reinsurance contracts and property valuation. Key Deliverables: The groups will prepare an Exposure Draft of RBC Regulations and an Approach Paper, supported by data, quantified impact assessments and sensitivity testing. Timeline: The two working groups have been given one month to complete their work and submit the required deliverables. Legal Framework: The working groups will examine whether the converged valuation framework should be adopted for actuarial valuation under Sections 13 and 49 of the Insurance Act, 1938, alongside solvency- related requirements and supervisory intervention provisions. About Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI): IRDAI was constituted in 1999 and was incorporated as a statutory body in April, 2000. It also operates under the powers of the Insurance Act, 1938.

AWARDS & RECOGNITIONS British Author M. John Harrison Wins 2026 Booker Prize for Novel ‘The End of Everything’ On 9 November 2026, British author M. John Harrison won the 2026 Booker Prize for his 13th novel, The End of Everything at a ceremony held at Old Billingsgate, London, United Kingdom (UK), becoming the first dedicated science fiction and speculative fiction author to win the prestigious award since its inception in 1969. • He received the Booker Prize trophy from David Szalay, the 2025 winner for his novel “Flesh.” • At 81, he became the oldest author to win the Booker Prize, surpassing the previous record held by Canadian author Margaret Atwood, who was 79 when she jointly won the 2019 Booker Prize for ‘The Testaments’. Exam Hints: ✓ What? 2026 Booker Prize Awarded ✓ Winner: M. John Harrison, British author (81 year) ✓ Winning Novel: The End of Everything. ✓ Distinction: Oldest author to win the Booker Prize. ✓ Prize Amount: 50,000 GBP ✓ Venue: Old Billingsgate, London, United Kingdom. ✓ Presenter: David Szalay (Winner – Booker Prize 2025) ✓ Judging Panel Chair: Dame Mary Beard.

# Page 21^page=21
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 21 Daily Content PDF About 2026 Booker Prize: Prize Money: M. John Harrison received a cash prize of British Pound Sterling (GBP) 50,000 (USD 67,000) along with a trophy. Judging Panel: The 2026 Booker Prize judging panel was chaired by Dame Mary Beard, a renowned classicist, historian and author and included Jarvis Cocker, Patricia Lockwood, Raymond Antrobus and Rebecca Liu. 2026 Booker Prize Shortlist: • The End of Everything by M. John Harrison (British Novelist) – Winner • The Disappearers by Marlon James (Jamaican Novelist) • John of John by Douglas Stuart (Scottish- American Novelist) • The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout (American Novelist) • Black Bag by Luke Kennard (British Novelist) • May We Feed the King by Rebecca Perry (British Novelist) About Novel ‘The End of Everything’: Overview: Published in 2026 by Serpent’s Tail (Profile Books), The End of Everything is a 198-page dystopian science fiction satire set in post-apocalyptic Britain, inspired by the 2008 global financial crisis, and marks the publisher’s first Booker Prize win.
